newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Yang Ming to order five new ships.
newsitem.headline: Yang Ming to order five new ships.

text.p: Taiwan's Yang Ming Marine Corp said on Friday it plans to order five new large-sized container ships which will cost more than US$300 million for its future expansion at year-end or early in 1997.

"We plan to order five new large-sized container ships, each with a loading capacity of some 5,000 twenty-foot-equivalent-unit (TEUs) either at year-end or early 1997," Yang Ming vice-president Tsai Ming-hsu told Reuters.
"Each ship is expected to cost more than $60 million, so the total will exceed $300 million," he said by telephone.
The company had yet to decide whether it would open an international or domestic bid for the order, Tsai said.
Building the ships would take about one year and 10 months, he said. "We expect to start using these new ships in early 1999," Tsai said.
Yang Ming had just issued global depositary receipts (GDRs) abroad to raise T$3.2 billion for building the new container ships, Tsai said.
The firm conducted a rights issue of 100 million shares, with each share priced at T$32.01, for the GDR issue, saving an annual interest cost of T$250 million for Yang Ming.
The company, one of Taiwan's biggest shipping firms, was privatised in February after an offer of 110 million shares, reducing the government's stake to 48 percent from 56.5 percent.
